scope: Bounded primary-source review for Hopf correspondence and the separately labeled candidate shared-reference view
execution_policy: Read-only source inspection. No upstream code execution, deployment, external communication, human study, or later gate execution.

primary_sources.title: Niles Johnson, A visualization of the Hopf fibration
pins: lines 0-4: S³ represented by circles over points of S²
lines 12-18: linked fibers, latitude tori, and two-solid-tori decomposition
lines 23-33: S³ in R⁴, circle fibers, and the exceptional line/circle through infinity
supported_statements: The Hopf fibration organizes S³ as circle fibers over S² base points.
Distinct fibers are linked, and fibers over latitude circles form tori.
The exceptional stereographic-looking central line closes as a circle through infinity in S³.
primary_sources.use_in_gate2: Visual and explanatory basis for selectable base/fiber views, the pole/infinity case, and finite-rendering caveats.

primary_sources.title: David W. Lyons, An Elementary Introduction to the Hopf Fibration
primary_sources.source_type: author mathematical exposition, Lebanon Valley College
pins: PDF pp. 2-3 / lines 50-64: quaternion-coordinate Hopf map S³→S² and unit-sphere image
PDF pp. 7-8 / lines 316-335: fibers are inverse images and each is a circle
PDF pp. 10-11 / lines 441-512: stereographic chart S³ minus one point to R³; fibers become circles or a line
PDF pp. 11-13 / lines 516-543, 613-616: exceptional axis and linked projected fibers
supported_statements: The Hopf map is a map from S³ to S² whose inverse image over a base point is a circle.
Stereographic projection omits one selected point of S³ and maps fibers to circles except for the fiber containing that point, which maps to a line.
The quaternion-coordinate convention must be recorded when comparing with a complex-pair convention.
primary_sources.use_in_gate2: Primary derivation for base/fiber identity, stereographic pole handling, and convention warning.

primary_sources.title: Ralph L. Cohen, The Topology of Fiber Bundles
pins: PDF pp. 14-18 / lines 521-590, 753-779: principal-bundle definition, S³→S² Hopf fibration
PDF p. 19 / lines 780-808: upper/lower hemisphere local trivializations
PDF pp. 19-20 / lines 829-839: principal bundle has a section iff it is trivial
PDF p. 20 / lines 840-865: overlap clutching/transition functions
supported_statements: The Hopf map is a principal S¹ bundle over S².
The bundle is locally trivial over two hemisphere charts.
A global section would trivialize a principal bundle, so the no-global-section claim must be tied to the Hopf bundle's nontriviality.
primary_sources.use_in_gate2: Needed university-hosted primary reference for local sections, transition functions, and the section/triviality implication.
